summary: Contestants demonstrate practical skills in configuring, maintaining, and troubleshooting devices as an IT technician. The event includes an objective test and, at Nationals, a certification exam and a performance component. Contestants may use written reference materials during some portions, and must follow specific equipment and eligibility rules.
time_limits: Preliminaries - No more than sixty (60) minutes for objective test
Preliminaries (Nationals only) - No more than sixty (60) minutes for objective test
Preliminaries (Nationals only) - No more than fifty (50) minutes for certification test
Preliminaries (Nationals only) - No more than sixty (60) minutes for performance component
Finals (Nationals only) - No more than sixty (60) minutes for performance component
what_to_bring: Published and/or unpublished non-electronic written reference materials, including hands-on tasks
(Optional) Cordless calculator: Electronic devices will be monitored according to ACT standards
competencies: Install, upgrade, and safely replace hardware components to maintain, optimize, and extend device performance and lifecycle
Identify and connect peripheral devices using the appropriate ports and interfaces, install and update device drivers, and diagnose and resolve connectivity, compatibility, and performance issues
Configure and manage storage devices and technologies, allocate and optimize system resources, and troubleshoot storage-related and resource-related performance issues
Diagnose hardware and software issues, troubleshoot boot procedures, and perform preventative maintenance to minimize downtime and ensure system reliability
Install, configure, and maintain Windows® and Linux operating systems and manage user accounts to support secure and efficient computing environments
Configure and manage cloud services and firewall settings to enable secure connectivity, data storage, and remote access
Configure, manage, and secure mobile devices using Mobile Device Management (MDM) tools to ensure consistent policies, data protection, and reliable access across enterprise environments
Use imaging and deployment tools to create, customize, and deploy operating system images, ensuring efficient setup, standardization, and rapid provisioning of client systems
Create, configure, and manage virtual machines for testing and troubleshooting, enabling safe experimentation, multi-OS environments, and flexible lab simulations
Identify, diagnose, and resolve connectivity, configuration, and security issues in Internet of Things (IoT) devices to ensure reliable integration within modern network environments
judging_notes: AI Policy Level 1 No AI Allowed
Previous Business Professionals of America tests and/or sample tests (handwritten, photocopied or keyed) may not be taken into the testing area. Violation of this rule will result in disqualification

At NLC, contestants will take IT Specialist Device Configuration and Management certification as part of the event. Contestants passing this certification will have 50 points added to their event score.
A Pearson profile must be created at https://certiport.pearsonvue.com before attending NLC
Contestants must include their BPA Contestant ID in their Pearson profile when they register
Certiport Parent/Legal Guardian Consent Form must be uploaded to: education@bpa.org
Reference materials are not allowed for certification testing

The top 10 contestants at Nationals will advance to a final round that includes a performance component. Scores from the preliminary round and the objective test will not carry over to the finals. Reference materials may be used during the application portion of the final round.
eligibility_notes: Any secondary or postsecondary division contestant may enter this objective event.
